site.name: stratabox
site.summary: stratabox-clone Fictional headless content platform "Stratabox" marketing site (Contentful / Sanity-style). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page long scroll: sticky top nav; hero with editor-vs-live-preview split panel that periodically swaps blocks; trusted-by logo strip; 4-stat row with intersection-observer count-up; 3 feature cards; **live block builder** (drag-and-drop reorder, type switcher, add/delete blocks, two-pane editor + render with debounced auto-save status); 4-language SDK code tabs (JS / Python / Ruby / curl) with copy button; 24-card searchable integrations grid; 3 customer quotes; gradient pricing teaser; dark 4-column footer | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E7E7E warm teal + cream paper; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 720–1100 / <720) | | `script.js` | Stat count-up via IntersectionObserver; hero block-swap micro-animation every 3.5s; full builder logic (reorder via HTML5 drag-and-drop, type switcher, add/delete, debounced auto-save status); SDK tab switcher with syntax-highlighted snippets and copy-to-clipboard toast; integrations search filter (matches name + category) with live count |

run_plan.goal: Critique the end-to-end UX of the stratabox marketing + interactive builder experience, with emphasis on the pricing section and adjacent flows (navigation, SDK tabs, integrations search, and key builder controls).
run_plan.summary: Run a full long-scroll exploration on index.html, validating sticky navigation anchors, the hero editor/live preview builder interactions, the SDK language tabs with copy behavior, and the integrations search/filter results. Then deep-dive on the pricing section to confirm plan navigation and CTAs, plus validate key mobile interactions and tap targets.
assumptions: All relevant functionality (builder, tabs, search, pricing) is contained on the single page index.html via anchors and in-page widgets.
Pricing CTAs (“See full plans →”, “Start free”, “Book a demo”) are actionable and should lead to meaningful in-page changes or modals.
The SDK code tabs include a working copy-to-clipboard toast/feedback mechanism.
risk_hotspots: Hero live block builder: drag-and-drop reorder + add/delete blocks + type switcher + debounced auto-save status (risk: state inconsistency, broken DnD, unclear save feedback)
LIVE PREVIEW modes (web / mobile / email) toggle visibility while hero content blocks are swapped (risk: preview not syncing, confusing mode switching)
SDK language code tabs (JS / Python / Ruby / curl) + copy-to-clipboard toast (risk: copy fails silently, wrong language shown, missing feedback)
Integrations searchable grid (search input “Search 24 visible integrations…” + live count) (risk: filtering incorrect, count mismatch, keyboard/focus issues)
Sticky top nav anchor links (Product/Builder/SDKs/Integrations/Customers/Pricing) with small mobile tap targets (risk: hard to tap, anchor offset issues)
Pricing section CTAs (“See full plans →”, plus “Start free” and “Book a demo”) (risk: unclear hierarchy, CTAs not leading anywhere, missing plan differentiation on mobile)

phases.title: Global navigation + anchor sanity
phases.objective: Verify sticky header behavior and anchor navigation to all major sections without losing context.
key_checks: Use top nav links (Product, Builder, SDKs, Integrations, Customers, Pricing) and confirm the page scrolls to the correct section headings.
Activate “Start free” and “Sign in” and verify whether they trigger a modal, navigate, or scroll (no dead-end).
On mobile viewport, attempt repeated tapping of small header links and confirm they are reliably clickable.
exit_criteria: All anchor links land at the intended sections (visually confirmed in-page).
CTAs for “Start free” and “Sign in” produce a clear outcome (modal/navigation/notice).
No broken navigation or unexpected scroll-jumps on mobile.

phases.title: Hero editor vs live preview builder interaction
phases.objective: Validate the core builder UX: adding, editing, deleting blocks, preview synchronization, and save feedback.
key_checks: Interact with editor block inputs: “New section heading”, “Body paragraph…”, and image alt/name fields (ux-18/ux-21/ux-24) and confirm changes appear in the live preview.
Use add controls for each block type (e.g., “+ Paragraph”, “+ Heading”, “+ Image”, “+ Callout”) and confirm the new block appears in EDITOR and updates the preview.
Reorder blocks via drag-and-drop and verify both editor order and live preview order reflect the change.
Switch a block type using the type switcher (where available) and confirm content/controls update and preview stays consistent.
Delete a block and verify the editor and preview remove it cleanly.
Observe debounced auto-save status near “saved” while editing; confirm feedback appears at least once and ends in a stable saved state.
exit_criteria: Editor edits propagate to live preview without noticeable lag or mismatch (including after reorder and type switch).
Add/delete actions are visually and functionally consistent.
Auto-save feedback is understandable and reaches a stable ‘saved’ state after interaction.

phases.title: SDK language tabs + copy feedback
phases.objective: Ensure SDK tab switching correctly updates code samples and copy actions provide reliable feedback.
key_checks: Switch SDK tabs across JS → Python → Ruby → curl and confirm code content changes accordingly.
Click the copy button for a tab and confirm clipboard copy succeeds or at least shows a visible success/failure toast.
After switching tabs, click copy again and verify the toast corresponds to the currently visible language.
exit_criteria: All tab switches update the displayed snippet accurately.
Copy-to-clipboard provides clear user feedback and operates on the active snippet.

phases.title: Integrations grid search + live count
phases.objective: Validate search/filter logic, result count accuracy, and input usability.
key_checks: Use the search input “Search 24 visible integrations…” (ux-38). Type a query matching by name and confirm the grid filters.
Type a query matching by category (if categories are indicated on cards) and confirm results update.
Clear the search and confirm the full set returns and the live count matches the number of visible cards.
On mobile viewport, focus the search input and verify soft keyboard usability and no layout overlap.
exit_criteria: Search results and the displayed count remain consistent for multiple queries.
Clearing search restores the full grid without UI glitches.
Mobile search focus and typing work smoothly.

phases.title: Pricing section deep-check + CTAs
phases.objective: Critically assess the pricing information architecture and confirm CTA pathways work.
key_checks: Jump to Pricing via nav and verify pricing teaser/plan content is readable and scannable.
Activate “See full plans →” and confirm what happens (scroll, modal, new content section).
Use pricing-adjacent CTAs (“Start free” and “Book a demo” if present near pricing) and verify outcomes are coherent and not duplicated or confusing.
On mobile viewport, verify pricing CTA tap targets and layout alignment (no overlaps, no truncated buttons).
exit_criteria: Pricing section contains actionable pathways with no dead-end interactions.
CTA outcomes are clear and consistent across desktop and mobile.
Mobile pricing layout remains usable (no broken wrapping/truncation of buttons).

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (index.html only).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise: hero builder add/edit/delete/reorder/type switch + saved status; preview mode toggling (web/mobile/email if interactive); SDK tab switching + copy; integrations search filtering + live count; pricing CTAs (“See full plans →”, “Start free”, “Book a demo”).
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (builder edits + save feedback, SDK copy, integrations search, and pricing CTAs + header anchor tapping) on mobile viewport.

notes: Because console/network errors are empty in the prescan, focus validation on UX state consistency rather than technical failures.
Treat the hero builder as the highest-risk interactive system: collect evidence for each action (before/after order, preview sync, and save status changes).
Keep step budget realistic: prioritize interactions that change state (builder DnD/add/delete/type switch, SDK copy, integrations filter, pricing CTA).

A headless content platform where editors author with composable blocks, developers query a typed GraphQL+REST API, and your team ships content to web, mobile, kiosks, and email — from a single source of truth. Start free → Book a demo ✔ 50 GB asset CDN free ✔ SOC 2 Type II ✔ EU + US regions studio.stratabox.dev / articles / coastal-bloom EDITOR ● saved H1 Coastal Bloom Returns ¶ After a two-year hiatus the festival returns to the Pier 22 boardwalk… ¶ Organizers expect twelve thousand visitors over the weekend… ▦ Gallery · 8 images ▣ hero-coast-2026.jpg · 4096×2304 ★ Callout · Tickets on sale May 22 LIVE PREVIEW web · mobile · email Coastal Bloom Returns After a two-year hiatus the festival returns to the Pier 22 boardwalk… hero-coast-2026.jpg ★ Tickets on sale May 22 Organizers expect twelve thousand visitors over the weekend… IN PRODUCTION AT Halcyon Northwind Atlas Bicycle Vesper Wine Riverbed Pinecrest Public Radio Holm & Brock Studio Nephele 2,400+ teams shipping content 99.99% trailing-90d API uptime 42ms p50 read latency 74 locales supported out of the box Platform Built around composable blocks. Editors compose pages from typed blocks. Developers consume the same blocks through a typed API. The platform handles versioning, scheduling, localization, previews, and asset delivery. ▣ Composable schema Define content types and blocks with a visual schema editor or by committing a schema.tb file. Migrations are diffed, reviewed, and rolled back per environment. Typed references & embeds Per-field localization Backward-compatible deprecations ⟳ Real-time collaboration Multi-cursor editing on every block. Suggestions, threads, and assignment live alongside the content. Conflict-free at the field level. Per-block presence Inline review & approval Slack, Linear, Jira mirrors ⚡ Edge content API Read your content from 280 edge POPs with stale-while-revalidate. GraphQL, REST, and a typed JS/TS client are all generated from the same schema. Per-environment tokens Preview & production fork Stable webhooks & replay Studio Drag, drop, ship. A headless content platform where editors author with composable blocks, developers query a typed GraphQL+REST API, and your team ships content to web, mobile, kiosks, and email — from a single source of truth. Editors compose pages from typed blocks. Developers consume the same blocks through a typed API. The platform handles versioning, scheduling, localization, previews, and asset delivery. ▣ Composable schema Define content types and blocks with a visual schema editor or by committing a schema.tb file. Migrations are diffed, reviewed, and rolled back per environment. Typed references & embeds Per-field localization Backward-compatible deprecations ⟳ Real-time collaboration Multi-cursor editing on every block. Suggestions, threads, and assignment live alongside the content. Conflict-free at the field level. Per-block presence Inline review & approval Slack, Linear, Jira mirrors ⚡ Edge content API Read your content from 280 edge POPs with stale-while-revalidate.
